headline: Australian Regulator Probes Collapse of Firmus's $5 Billion Data Center IPO
summary: Australia’s corporate regulator is investigating the failed $5 billion initial public offering of Firmus. The planned listing collapsed on October 9 after failing to secure sufficient investor backing.
why: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission monitors capital markets integrity and disclosure compliance for domestic IPOs.

impacts.name: Data Centers
impacts.why: Regulatory scrutiny following a collapsed $5 billion deal dampens investor appetite for regional data center listings.
